places.name: Henniker, New Hampshire
places.what: Born Amy Marcy Cheney. At four she composed three waltzes in her head during a summer on her grandfather’s farm in West Henniker, where there was no piano. Coordinates mark the town.

sources.title: Cheryl Gillard, ‘Beach, Amy Cheney’, Women in World History (Encyclopedia.com)

places.name: Chelsea, Massachusetts
places.what: The Cheneys moved here in 1871, when Amy was four. At six she began piano lessons with her mother.

sources.title: Cheryl Gillard, ‘Beach, Amy Cheney’, Women in World History (Encyclopedia.com)

places.name: Boston, Massachusetts
places.what: The family moved to Boston in 1875. She studied piano with Ernst Perabo and Carl Baermann and harmony with Junius Hill, and was kept from European study. Coordinates mark the city.

sources.title: Chamber Music Society of Lincoln Center: Amy Beach (1867–1944), biography

places.name: Boston Music Hall
places.what: Her public debut as a pianist was at A. P. Peck’s Anniversary Concert, in Moscheles’s G minor Concerto and Chopin’s E♭ Rondo. The hall on Winter Street still stands; its interior was rebuilt as the Orpheum Theatre.

places.name: 28 Commonwealth Avenue, Boston
places.what: Dr Beach had owned this Back Bay house since 1879, and she moved in when they married in December 1885. After his death in 1910 she let it to physicians; she sold it in 1924.

places.what: The sonata was first played at the Kneisel Quartet’s fourth concert, with Mrs Beach assisting. The hall stood at the corner of Boylston and Berkeley Streets, and the coordinates mark that corner.

places.name: Centerville, Cape Cod
places.what: After her husband’s funeral she and her mother went to her cottage here, which remained her main summer residence. It had been paid for with the royalties from her song Ecstasy.

places.name: Dresden
places.what: At her European concert debut she played her Violin Sonata with a violinist named Dr Bülau. From the autumn of 1912 she played her concerto, sonata and quintet in German cities.

places.name: Munich
places.what: Photographed here by H. Wiedenmann with the soprano Marcella Craft of the Munich opera, who had sung her songs in European recitals.

places.name: Hamburg
places.what: She played her Piano Concerto with a Hamburg orchestra, and the “Gaelic” Symphony was performed. Dr Ferdinand Pfohl reviewed the concert in the Hamburger Nachrichten of 3 December 1913.

sources.title: Eugene Gates, ‘Mrs. H. H. A. Beach: American Symphonist’, The Kapralova Society Journal 8:2 (Fall 2010)

places.name: Rome
places.what: She sailed on 11 December 1928 for a five-month trip. In Rome she finished her String Quartet, Op. 89, sketched at the MacDowell Colony in 1921, and appeared in concerts at the American Academy and the American embassy.

sources.title: Cheryl Gillard, ‘Beach, Amy Cheney’, Women in World History (Encyclopedia.com)

places.name: MacDowell Colony, Peterborough, New Hampshire
places.what: Eighteen residencies in the Watson studio. In 1921 she took down hermit thrush songs here for her Op. 92 pieces.
